restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r3-prefix-v1 only (three partial rounds plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction uses the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

Success probability 1 means: one deterministic procedure (centres c_i = i tried in the order i = 1, 2, 3, ... until the first verified collision, at most 64 trials) was executed once from the start on the fixed target and stopped with a collision after 1 trial(s); the time is the executed operation count of that run with every trial charged, and the memory is the whole static executable image plus a 64 KiB stack bound (above the measured peak resident set). It is not a probability over centres; nothing was selected beforehand.
The collision found is the same pair as the certificate of edd943c (same line j = 0 and centre c = 1); the claim is the executed cost of this independently written program.

heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 describe the executed program of proof.md section 9 under the stated rules: 1 per canonical field addition, subtraction, multiplication or squaring (a Montgomery conversion is one multiplication; inversion and exponentiation expanded per bit), 1 per 256-bit element load or store plus 1 address operation, 3 per loop iteration plus 2 per loop exit, 1 per other executed integer or control operation, 279 per line evaluation and per reference permutation, stated constant bounds for stage bookkeeping, the prologue and the report/system calls, and a register file of 18 words of 256 bits (8 data words, 7 twiddles or constants and one temporary per transform block), with integer indices, pointers and loop bounds in integer registers and procedure calls treated as inlined.
heuristics.scope: All stages of the executed run at the target dimensions: m = 976562; line interpolation on 2^20 points (2^21 line evaluations); stage C transforms of size 2^20 on H_20 and its coset, 237 steps; stage D products on 3 * 2^(j-2) or 2^j points.
heuristics.extrapolation: None. The time is the executed total of one run of the shipped source, with every trial charged and stages H and I included; the only bounds in it are the stated constants (proof.md section 4.2).
heuristics.limitations: The counts are produced by the instrumentation written into the source; the source is part of the proof text (it rebuilds to the byte-identical counted binary) and was not run by the organizer, so the time bound also rests on the faithful execution of that deterministic source (about 15 minutes on one core). Word-level costs outside the stated rules (cache, bandwidth) are not part of the model. Sensitivity to the register premise (rough estimate from the pass structure): with about 8 registers (radix-4 blocks) stage C would cost roughly +0.13 in time_log2, and with no multi-word blocks (radix-2) roughly +0.5.
